entries.summary: Render an absent value in user-facing output as a designed token; never let a raw undefined, null, or empty slot reach the user.
body: Batch 11 task 2: a stamp without a version field made update print `kit undefined -> 0.1.0`, and a test pinned the artifact as contract. The guard's real guarantee was that version may be absent, so absence needed a designed rendering: `kit none -> <running>`.

Decide each field's absent case at design time. Absence that is legitimate gets a named token. A value that is present but invalid is not absence: reject it before any write, the way idPrefix and version raise UsageError.
A leaked `undefined` or `NaN` in output is always a finding, even when disclosed and tested; the test moves to the designed output, never pins the leak.
Root-only entry: the seed ships no cli area, so this loads here through area cli and is not seeded.

source.ref: batch 11 branch review, uncovered finding; task 2 review r0

entries.summary: When behavior changes, update every user-facing surface that states it (help, errors, documented procedures) and verify a procedure by following it as printed.
body: Help output, error messages, and documented step sequences are contract surfaces the way exported symbols are; a behavior fix that leaves them stating the old behavior ships the old defect to the user in prose form.
Enumerate the surfaces mechanically: grep the user-visible strings for the changed concept (the old flag, shape, or step) rather than recalling where it is mentioned.

A documented procedure is verified by executing its printed steps in order, on the environment it targets or the closest disclosed proxy; a paraphrase check misses preconditions the source text carries.

Batch-27 retrospective: the surface list for a CLI change includes --help for every touched subcommand and every printed receipt line; run the command and read its own output as a user before closing the task. Both batch-27 instances were surfaces the implementer never re-read after the behavior moved (update's about text; a receipt line update never prints).

When a configuration key gains a second consumer, sweep the texts that define the key, not only the texts of the command that changed (batch 28: `overrides` also decides which kit-owned files check-knowledge reads, and the seeded docs/README.md that defines the key was outside the sweep).

When a change alters which inputs reach an existing error path, re-read every message on that path with the new inputs and name each case. A message that misstates the cause for a newly reachable input is a contract defect, even when the refusal is right (batch 32 task 1: `unknown id` for a known controller entry).

entries.summary: A lint whose subject is a delimited token matches the token and its delimiters with one pattern; it pairs no delimiters and models no document around it.
body: Batch 28 task 6 needed three designs for one extractor: knowledge ids in backticks in kit-owned markdown. Per-line pairing lost every id after a code span that wraps a line. Whole-text pairing lost every id after one stray backtick. The third design pairs nothing: a backtick, the id pattern of the schema, and a lookahead for a backtick.

Pairing delimiters is parsing. A parser for the enclosing format needs the block rules of that format, and a hand-written subset fails on the first input outside it. Use a maintained parser, which is a dependency the owner rules, or define the subject so that no parser is needed.

State the limits of the token form in the module doc and pin each with a test: the text that is not extracted (a padded or wrapped token) and the text that is extracted although a renderer shows no span.

A reviewer who proposes the fix design runs it against the classes of the reviewer's own counter-example before filing (process.review-findings-are-claims-too). The round-0 proposal to pair as CommonMark does became the round-1 regression.

source.ref: batch 28 branch review; task 6 rounds 0 to 2

entries.summary: A test that pins 'this and nothing else' on a contract surface compares the whole structure and proves each forbidden shape with a mutation.
body: A presence check pins presence. It passes when a second trigger, permission, or key stands beside the pinned one (batch 30 task 1: four forbidden shapes passed three pins of a workflow).

Keep the forbidden shapes as a permanent table in the test, and add the harmless edits too (a comment, a reordered key): a pin that fails for a harmless edit is as wrong as one that passes a forbidden shape.
A hand-written reader of a file format is part of the pin: mutate around its limits (comment lines, blank lines, key order).
Narrowed at batch 33's close (stats: 3 of 3 findings minor or on a deliverable): the rule governs contract surfaces, such as CLI output, a schema, or a generated file.

source.ref: batch 30: the task review's issue 2; the branch review's issues 8 and 9

entries.summary: Walk a step that selects a resource and acts on it through each state the resource can have when read: gone, merged, failing, edited, stale in the listing.
body: The walk of process.gates-cover-generated-commits covers who writes a commit and which resources a step creates. A step that picks one item from a list has a third axis: the state of the item.

For each state, write what the step does and what it costs per run. A state that keeps the item selected on every run is a limit; state it with its cost, or change the selection (batch 30, argued in the branch review and not observed: a pull request with a failed check would stay the lowest-numbered candidate on every push; the owner ruled that the step skips it).
